name: No cycle
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: None. Every edge goes from a smaller number to a bigger one, so no route can come back.

name: Two ways to one place
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: None. 3 is reached twice, from 1 and from 2, but that is not a cycle. Only an edge back to a vertex still on the current path closes a cycle; 3 is already finished (lesson 4).

name: An edge to itself
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: [1] is a cycle of one edge, from 1 to 1.

name: There and back
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: [0, 2]. In a directed graph, two edges in opposite directions make a cycle.

name: A cycle 0 cannot reach
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: [3, 4]. Start a search from every vertex that is not yet visited, not only from 0.

name: A cycle after a finished part
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: [3, 4, 5]. The search first finishes 2 and 1; reaching 2 again from 3 is not a cycle, but 5 → 3 is.

name: 1,000 vertices
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: a random graph with this many edges almost surely has a cycle. Any cycle is accepted.

name: A path of 100,000 with an edge back
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True: the cycle 50000 … 99999 has 50,000 vertices. A recursive search goes 100,000 calls deep and fails; keep your own stack (lesson 3).

name: 40 layers of two
args: (80, [(2 * i + a, 2 * i + 2 + b) for i in range(39) for a in range(2) for b in range(2)])
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
show: 40 layers of 2 vertices, every vertex joined to both in the next layer
why: None. There are 2⁴⁰ different paths from the top to the bottom. A search that forgets finished vertices walks all of them; with three states each vertex is finished once (lesson 4).

name: 100,000 vertices, no cycle
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
show: 100,000 vertices, 200,000 edges, each from a smaller number to a bigger one
why: None: every edge goes up, so there is no cycle. Each vertex and each edge must be handled once.

name: 100,000 vertices with cycles
expr: (lambda c: None if c is None else is_cycle(args[0], args[1], c))(find_cycle(args[0], list(args[1])))
why: True. Any cycle is accepted; the check follows your cycle's edges.
